name: Largo do Carmo
description: A small square in Chiado beside the roofless ruins of the Carmo Convent, wrecked in the 1755 earthquake. The 1974 revolution ended here.

name: Praça do Comércio
description: The big riverside square rebuilt after the 1755 earthquake, with yellow arcades on three sides and a triumphal arch leading into the Baixa.

name: Praça dos Restauradores
description: A square with an obelisk marking Portugal’s 1640 break from Spanish rule, at the foot of the Avenida da Liberdade.

name: São Jorge Castle
places: São Jorge Castle (Castelo de São Jorge)
description: The hilltop castle above Alfama, with walls and towers to walk and views over the city and the river.

name: Rossio
description: The old town’s main square, with wave-patterned paving, two fountains and the national theatre on its north side.

name: São Domingos Church
places: Largo de São Domingos (1506 massacre memorial)
description: A church left scarred by a 1959 fire, and the small square beside it with a memorial to the Jews killed in the 1506 massacre.

name: Praça Luís de Camões
description: A square between Chiado and Bairro Alto, with a statue of the poet Luís de Camões in the middle.

name: Fado Museum
description: A museum of fado, Lisbon’s song of longing, at the edge of Alfama, with guitars, recordings and portraits of singers.

name: A Brasileira
description: A café in Chiado open since 1905, with a dark wood interior and a bronze statue of the poet Fernando Pessoa at a table outside.

name: National Pantheon
description: A domed baroque church that took nearly 300 years to finish, now the resting place of national figures, including the fado singer Amália Rodrigues.

name: Santa Luzia viewpoint
description: A terrace beside a small church in Alfama, with tiled panels on the walls and a view over the rooftops to the river.

name: 25 de Abril Bridge
description: The red suspension bridge over the Tagus, opened in 1966 and renamed after the 1974 revolution.

name: Mercado da Ribeira
description: The city’s old riverside market hall, with fresh produce stalls on one side and a big food hall of restaurant counters on the other.

name: Jerónimos Monastery
description: A huge 16th-century monastery in Belém, carved in the ornate Manueline style, with the tomb of Vasco da Gama.

name: Monument to the Discoveries
description: A 52-metre monument on the Belém riverfront, shaped like a ship’s prow, lined with figures from Portugal’s age of exploration.

name: Maritime Museum
description: A museum of Portuguese seafaring in a wing of the Jerónimos Monastery, with model ships, maps, instruments and royal barges.

name: Gulbenkian Museum
description: An art museum in a modernist building and garden, with one man’s collection running from ancient Egypt to art nouveau jewellery.
